entities.name: Shōji Hamada
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Shōji Hamada  was a Japanese potter. He had a significant influence on studio pottery of the twentieth century, and a major figure of the mingei (folk-art) movement, establishing the town of Mashiko as a pottery centre. In 1955 he was designated a "Living National Treasure".
